newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

A firmer New York market boosted London robusta futures prices. November ended $20 up at $1,524, failing to hold onto a high of $1,527. In New York arabica futures advanced further, although the upside was curbed and it appeared buying interest was beginning to ebb. There was hardly any news and the market is not likely to find the same upward thrust as it did a month ago when it was rallying against tight supplies for the now expired September position, traders said.

The market's ability to hold present levels should rest on the ACPC's ability to keep exports limited in the months ahead, it was added. ICO meetings are presently going on and then the ACPC meeting will follow on Friday and Saturday. There is talk that Vietnam might be interested in joining, which might be mildly supportive for the market.

NICARAGUA - According to industry sources, coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) is likely to reach 767,000 60-kg bags, down from 822,000 bags estimated earlier and last year's production of 921,000 bags. Of the total produced in 1996/97, 633,000 bags are expected to be exported.

HONDURAS - Coffee exports in 1995/96 (October/September) reached 2.066 million 60-kg bags, up from 1.636 million bags exported the previous year, the Honduran Coffee Institute (IHCAFE) said. Despite higher exports, revenues fell to $269.4 million from $283.0 million because of lower world market prices. About 75,000 Honduran coffee producers make coffee the second most important export after bananas.

DENMARK - Denmark imported 91,894 bags of coffee in June 1996, 11 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 511,000 bags, 30.5 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 14 per cent to 873,700 bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Brazil (121,700 vs 147,700 bags) and Colombia (113,100 vs 88,100 bags). The country exported 47,600 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 15 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.5 per cent to 91,200 bags.
